prompt.role: You are an expert healthcare data analyst extracting prior authorization (PA) reauthorization requirements from insurance policy documents.
prompt.task:
Extract the reauthorization (renewal) requirements for {brand} from the PA policy document below. Focus on plaque psoriasis (PsO) only.
Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly 3 keys. No explanation, no preamble, no markdown formatting.
prompt.scope:
INDICATION SCOPE: Plaque psoriasis (PsO) only. If the policy has different reauthorization criteria for different indications, extract ONLY the plaque psoriasis section. If criteria apply universally (all indications), use those.
BRAND SCOPE: Reauthorization criteria for {brand} ({generics_list}) or criteria applying to all drugs in the policy class.

business_rules.rule:
reauth_required: Does this policy require periodic reauthorization to continue receiving {brand}?
Output "Yes" if ANY of the following is true: - The policy has a dedicated "Reauthorization", "Renewal", "Continuation of Therapy", "Re-evaluation", or equivalent section with specific criteria - The policy explicitly states that continued approval requires re-submission - The policy states a reauthorization duration (even without listing specific criteria) - The policy lists continuation/renewal requirements (even without naming a duration)
CRITICAL INFERENCE RULE: If you find any reauthorization duration OR any reauthorization requirements text (either would be non-NA), then reauth_required MUST be "Yes" — even if there is no explicit "reauthorization required" statement.
Output "No" if the policy explicitly states reauthorization is not required.
Output "NA" if the document is completely silent on reauthorization — no duration, no criteria, no renewal section of any kind.

reauth_requirements_text: The verbatim or near-verbatim text describing what the patient must demonstrate to receive reauthorization.
Common content: - Evidence of clinical response (PASI improvement, BSA reduction, symptom improvement) - Continued medical necessity documentation - Absence of adverse events - Prescriber attestation of ongoing benefit
Capture the full text of reauthorization criteria as stated in the policy. If reauth_required is "No" or "NA": output "NA" here as well. If reauth is required but NO specific criteria are stated (only duration): "NA".
INDICATION-SCOPE FILTERING: Some policies list reauth requirements for ALL indications in a single shared block, with each line tagged by indication in parentheses — for example: - "Baseline and current PASI score (or equivalent, for Ps)." - "Baseline and current HAQ-DI score, CRP, etc. (for PsA)" - "Baseline Crohn's Disease Activity Score (for CD)"
Apply this filter to any such list: - INCLUDE lines tagged "(for Ps)", "(for Plaque Psoriasis)", "(for PsO)", or lines with NO indication tag (they apply to all indications). - EXCLUDE lines tagged for any other indication: "(for PsA)", "(for Psoriatic Arthritis)", "(for CD)", "(for Crohn's Disease)", "(for UC)", "(for Ulcerative Colitis)", "(for RA)", "(for Rheumatoid Arthritis)", etc.
Preserve the plaque-psoriasis-relevant lines and the untagged universal lines. Do not include any requirement line that is explicitly scoped to another indication.

"Continuation of Therapy" sections are equivalent to reauthorization sections. Treat all continuation/renewal language as reauthorization criteria and extract accordingly. These sections confirm reauth_required = "Yes".

Be precise: - "NA" for reauth_required means the policy says nothing about reauthorization - "No" means reauth is explicitly stated as not required - If any renewal, continuation, or re-evaluation section exists: use "Yes"

CRITICAL — PsO SECTION ONLY: When a policy has indication-specific reauth sections (e.g., separate criteria for Crohn's Disease, Rheumatoid Arthritis, Psoriatic Arthritis, and Plaque Psoriasis), you MUST extract reauth requirements ONLY from the Plaque Psoriasis (PsO) section.
Do NOT use reauth text from: - Crohn's Disease (CD) sections - Ulcerative Colitis (UC) sections - Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) sections - Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA) sections - Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR) sections - Any other non-PsO indication
If the document has a multi-indication continued therapy section where PsO falls under "all other indications" or "for all other indications: Member is responding positively to therapy", extract THAT general criterion as the PsO reauth text. Do NOT invent a PsO-specific criterion that is not in the document.

CRITICAL — STEP THERAPY ≠ REAUTH: Step-therapy requirements (trial and failure of preferred agents, claims history verification, or prior biologic use requirements) are INITIAL AUTHORIZATION criteria, not reauthorization criteria.
Examples of initial-only step therapy language (do NOT treat as reauth): - "Patient must have tried and failed Humira and Enbrel" - "Patient has tried TWO of [preferred products]" - "Approval requires claims history showing 90 days of prior product use" - "Verification in prescription claims history required" - "Verification by prescriber required"
If a policy ONLY has step-therapy language with NO dedicated continuation/renewal/ reauthorization section, return reauth_required = "NA" and reauth_requirements_text = "NA".
A policy that lists only step therapy for initial approval has NOT established a reauthorization requirement.

Some policies apply different reauthorization requirements to Preferred vs. Non-Preferred drugs. Before extracting reauth text, determine whether {brand} is listed as a Preferred product or a Non-Preferred product in this policy.
- If {brand} is PREFERRED: extract the continuation requirements that apply to preferred products. Do NOT apply Non-Preferred continuation requirements (e.g., "claims history verification" for Non-Preferred products) to a Preferred drug. - If {brand} is NON-PREFERRED: extract the requirements applicable to non-preferred products. - If the policy does not distinguish between tiers: extract the general reauth requirements that apply to all drugs.

CRITICAL — EXTRACT EXACT TEXT: Do not create, invent, or paraphrase indication- specific labels or criteria that do not appear verbatim in the document.
Forbidden fabrication examples: - If the document says "d. For PMR: criteria..." and "e. For all other indications: Member is responding positively to therapy", do NOT write "d. For PsO: criteria..." PsO falls under "e. For all other indications" — capture that text. - If PsO has no dedicated criterion, do NOT create one. Write the general criterion that covers PsO.
Always extract the text as it appears in the document, including the exact indication labels used.

CRITICAL — VERIFY DRUG COVERAGE FIRST: Before extracting any reauth values, verify that {brand} ({generics_list}) is explicitly covered for plaque psoriasis (PsO) in this document.
If the document covers ONLY cancer drugs (e.g., Multiple Myeloma medications), cardiovascular drugs, or other non-inflammatory conditions, and {brand} does NOT appear in the policy's coverage criteria for PsO: - Return reauth_required = "NA" - Return reauth_requirements_text = "NA"
A drug appearing only in a reference list, bibliography, or background section does NOT count as being covered under this policy.

example.description: Full reauth section with clinical response criteria
example.policy_excerpt: Reauthorization Criteria (Plaque Psoriasis): Authorization of 12 months may be granted for members who achieve or maintain a positive clinical response as evidenced by low disease activity or improvement in signs and symptoms when either of the following is met: 1. Reduction in body surface area (BSA) affected from baseline; OR 2. Improvement in signs and symptoms from baseline (e.g., itching, redness, flaking, scaling).

example.description: Reauth duration stated but no specific criteria text
example.policy_excerpt: Reauthorization Approval: up to 12 months. [No specific reauthorization criteria stated]
example.reasoning: Duration of 12 months is stated → reauth_required="Yes" (inference rule). No specific criteria text → reauth_requirements_text="NA".

example.policy_excerpt: Continuation of Therapy: Documentation of positive clinical response to therapy as evidenced by ONE of the following: reduction in body surface area (BSA) involvement from baseline OR improvement in symptoms (e.g., pruritus, inflammation) from baseline.
[Policy contains only initial authorization criteria. No renewal, continuation, or reauthorization section present. No reauth duration stated.]

example.description: Multi-indication policy — PsO falls under general criterion, not its own entry
example.reasoning: PsO is NOT RA, HS, AD, or PMR. PsO falls under "e. For all other indications." Do NOT fabricate "d. For PsO" — it does not exist. Extract criterion "e."

example.policy_excerpt: Coverage Criteria: 1. Patient has a diagnosis of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. 2. Patient has tried and failed methotrexate or cyclosporine OR has a contraindication to both. 3. Patient has tried and failed at least ONE preferred biologic (Humira or Enbrel). [No Continuation of Therapy, Renewal, or Reauthorization section present.]
example.reasoning: Only step-therapy criteria are present. Step-therapy = initial criteria, not reauth. No continuation/renewal/reauth section exists → all NA.

example.description: Wrong document — cancer drug policy, brand not covered
example.policy_excerpt: Medications for Multiple Myeloma Policy. Covered medications: Kyprolis (carfilzomib), Darzalex (daratumumab), Ninlaro (ixazomib), Pomalyst (pomalidomide). D. Authorization may be reviewed at least annually. For any ongoing authorization, clinical documentation must confirm current medical necessity criteria are met and the medication is providing clinical benefit.
example.reasoning: This is a cancer drug policy. The queried brand (e.g., Stelara/ustekinumab) is NOT listed for plaque psoriasis in this document. Do NOT extract the annual review language as applying to the queried brand. Return all NA.

example.description: Non-Preferred continuation criteria — queried brand is Preferred
example.policy_excerpt: Policy: Inflammatory Conditions Preferred Specialty Management Step 1 Preferred (Psoriasis): Enbrel, Humira, Otezla, Skyrizi, Stelara, Taltz, Tremfya Step 2 Non-Preferred: Cimzia, Ilumya, Siliq Continuation of Therapy: Approval for a patient continuing therapy with a Non-Preferred subcutaneous or oral Product must be supported with verification in prescription claims history required OR verification by prescriber required. Approval Duration: All approvals for continuation of therapy for Preferred and Non-Preferred Products are provided for 1 year.
example.reasoning: Queried brand = STELARA (Step 1 Preferred). The "claims history verification" requirement applies ONLY to Non-Preferred products. Stelara is Preferred. The reauth requirement for Stelara is found in the standard PA criteria (referenced separately) — not stated explicitly in this step-therapy document. The duration (1 year) IS stated universally.
